chunks: And from him, from Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a free woman who is under the ownership of a male slave, and she buys him (to free him). Does his marriage become void? He said, 'Yes, because he is a slave who is unable to possess anything.'

key_terms.لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ: Unable to possess anything (referring to property/wealth)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a slave if his free wife buys and frees him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a free woman’s purchase of her slave husband does not automatically annul their marriage, as the slave remains under his master's authority and lacks independent legal capacity (*aqd*) to maintain the contract. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between the slave's personal status and his master's property rights, emphasizing that the bond persists unless the master explicitly dissolves it or grants full emancipation with independent agency. The reference to the slave's inability to 'do anything' underscores the classical concept of *abd* as a dependent entity in civil transactions.
